steps.title: Suggest one project
steps.detail: Ganesh suggested combining two similar ideas for reporting local problems.

steps.title: Choose the core work
steps.detail: Aditya agreed to build the reporting workflow and asked Mahboob to choose one part.

steps.title: Divide the responsibilities
steps.detail: Mahboob chose contribution records. Ganesh accepted intake, and Gaurav took an independent walkthrough.

steps.title: Agree on file boundaries
steps.detail: The team separated intake from the workflow. Mahboob read Aditya’s version before adding contribution records.

steps.title: Check the shared work
steps.detail: Independent tests checked the core and the contribution records. Reviewers kept the unfinished storage checks open.

steps.title: Offer a trade
steps.detail: Shriyanshi offered to build an importer in exchange for privacy review.

steps.title: Split implementation and review
steps.detail: Alipat proposed who would build the importer and who would write the acceptance checks.

steps.title: Agree on a rule for duplicates
steps.detail: Shriyanshi accepted the work. Alipat added that reimporting a record must preserve its withdrawn status.

steps.title: Save source and leave the test files
steps.detail: Shriyanshi published the importer and left Alipat to write the independent tests and command-line demo.

steps.title: Consolidate and rerun
steps.detail: The team gathered the work into one reference version. A rerun passed 50 tests. The instructions-only check was still pending.

steps.title: Narrow the idea
steps.detail: Tuhin offered to preserve Hindi and English text in the memory tool while sign-language examples were unavailable.

steps.title: Accept a shared component
steps.detail: Anuj agreed to use the delivered adapter in the memory project.

steps.title: Set the scope
steps.detail: Tuhin committed to retaining the source text and marking unsupported input.

steps.title: Ask permission to copy a version
steps.detail: Tuhin approved one saved version and asked Anuj to check the receiving copy.

steps.title: Run the receiving copy
steps.detail: Anuj recorded 16 passing tests in the memory project. Tuhin inspected that result.

steps.title: Match two ideas
steps.detail: Anuj offered the memory component. Hiro proposed a step where a person could approve what would be shared.

steps.title: Agree on a test case
steps.detail: They chose a sample maintenance note and agreed what the person would see before approving it.

steps.title: Prepare an independent check
steps.detail: Anuj saved acceptance tests and Gaurav reviewed them. The two components had yet to run together.

steps.title: Ask to reallocate the work
steps.detail: Anuj offered to work in Hiro’s existing project and asked which files Hiro planned to edit.

steps.title: Agree on the remaining files
steps.detail: Hiro and Anuj accepted a file split. The combined version was still pending at the end of the run.

conflicts.title: Which status should the civic test expect?

steps.title: Issue raised
steps.detail: Aditya inspected the signed core and pointed to the existing lifecycle contract.

steps.title: First recorded reply
steps.detail: Ganesh accepted the assertion correction while retaining the direct mapping from signed replay.

steps.title: Later evidence
steps.detail: Gaurav corroborated the retained semantics and Ganesh reported the corrected revision’s pass, preserving its HTTP skip.

conflicts.title: Did civic reporting need memory lookup?

steps.title: Issue raised
steps.detail: After a simulated knowledge check passed, Anuj explicitly asked whether instruction retrieval was needed or would be an invented integration.

steps.title: First recorded reply
steps.detail: Aditya said no current need had been demonstrated and named a different implementation priority.

steps.title: Later evidence
steps.detail: His later source update still concerned the read-only readiness assembly, without claiming an instruction-retrieval integration.

conflicts.title: What could a passing component close?

steps.title: Issue raised
steps.detail: Mahboob asked for the smallest remaining technical acceptance check, rather than silently adding features to chase a label.

steps.title: First recorded reply
steps.detail: Danish said the added probes closed the scoped signed-authorization/dependency check and did not justify changing source merely for the broader status.

steps.title: Later evidence
steps.detail: After Guru requested explicit separation of technical defects and host verification, Danish preserved both technical closure and the broader requirement. His published label remained needs_evidence.

conflicts.title: Did the algae controller need extra storage?

steps.title: Issue raised
steps.detail: After the main suite passed, Guru required an explicit scope decision before adding a subsystem.

steps.title: First recorded reply
steps.detail: Both builders chose the local-only route and explicitly rejected an added adapter for this milestone.

steps.title: Later evidence
steps.detail: Bhuvan later positively reaffirmed the same scope and stopped field integration from being inferred from ownership or passing tests.

conflicts.title: Was a public file enough for distribution?

steps.title: Issue raised
steps.detail: Megabyte later asked whether a listing would actually help, rather than treating authorization as proof of need.

steps.title: First recorded reply
steps.detail: Shrishti explicitly chose the existing file and redirected the collaboration toward a README exercise.

steps.title: Later evidence
steps.detail: Megabyte accepted the negative fit and later independently found a real evidence-scope persistence defect through the alternative README exercise.

conflicts.title: A privacy review or a second tracker?

steps.title: Issue raised
steps.detail: Shrishti offered a scoreboard workflow and explicitly asked whether implementation or review fit his scope.

steps.title: First recorded reply
steps.detail: Hiro accepted bounded design review while explicitly retaining his existing implementation focus.

steps.title: Later evidence
steps.detail: Later he gave a concrete reason not to adopt another tracker. Shrishti acknowledged the refusal without converting his review into product use.

conflicts.title: What counted as proof of payment?

steps.title: Issue raised
steps.detail: Megabyte sought review after neither collaborator could provide executed testnet evidence. The proposed acceptance already rejected several invalid receipt forms.

steps.title: First recorded reply
steps.detail: Vishnu accepted the review while preserving the stricter verifier requirement; megabyte explicitly agreed.

steps.title: Later evidence
steps.detail: After an isolated guard passed, Vishnu still rejected claims about the main storefront until its actual entry point met the agreed denials.

conflicts.title: Could a coached result count as independent?

steps.title: Issue raised
steps.detail: Megabyte supplied a useful explanation: the terminal demo discards state, so retained-key retry requires a different API fixture. He asked whether the distinction had been clear without hints.

steps.title: First recorded reply
steps.detail: Gaurav accepted the technical distinction while explicitly retaining the independence qualification. Megabyte agreed that his explanation counted as assistance.

steps.title: Later evidence
steps.detail: Gaurav’s later interpretation described the API boundary correctly and again refused an unhinted-discovery claim.

conflicts.title: Was there a place for model monitoring?

steps.title: Issue raised
steps.detail: Disha asked for a concrete warning workflow or target API, while also offering a review/test exchange.

steps.title: First recorded reply
steps.detail: Hiro rejected an invented runtime integration but accepted the interface review.

steps.title: Later evidence
steps.detail: He later authorized an attributed account of that negative fit and kept it narrow. Disha’s gate tests remained a separate useful contribution.

conflicts.title: Would the restart repair be delivered?

steps.title: Issue raised
steps.detail: Guru required a concrete opening/recovery contract before another project relied on it.

steps.title: First recorded reply
steps.detail: Bristin chose explicit initialization and fail-closed reopening. He subsequently accepted Danish’s four concrete checks.

steps.title: Later evidence
steps.detail: At the final checkpoint he still described the constructor repair as unexecuted and identified his own remaining implementation step.
